questions.q: Why does this lesson say alerting on every available metric is the wrong instinct?
options: A metric existing doesn't mean a deviation in it matters, and an unnecessary alert just teaches people to ignore alerts
Azure and AWS charge extra for every alert rule configured
Alerting on every metric is technically impossible to configure
Only security teams are allowed to configure alerts
questions.explain: The real skill is picking the small number of alerts tied to something a person genuinely needs to know about and can act on.

questions.q: What are the three categories of alert this lesson says actually matter for a new deployment?
options: Resource thresholds, failed health checks, and security-relevant events
Billing alerts, uptime alerts, and backup alerts
Network alerts, storage alerts, and compute alerts
Daily alerts, weekly alerts, and monthly alerts
questions.explain: Almost every alert worth having falls into one of these three buckets: resource thresholds, failed health checks, or security-relevant events.

questions.q: In the worked example, why is the CPU alert set to "above 85% for 15 minutes" rather than firing on any CPU spike?
options: To catch a runaway process or undersized VM rather than a brief, normal spike
Because Azure and AWS don't support shorter time windows
Because 15 minutes is the maximum alert duration allowed
To make sure the alert never actually fires
questions.explain: A sustained threshold filters out brief normal spikes and only flags CPU usage that's a genuine, lasting problem.

questions.q: What does the low-disk-space alert in the worked example directly address?
options: The exact disk-fills-up failure mode from Lesson 13, giving time to act before the disk is full
A security-relevant event like a failed login
A load balancer health check failure
A billing threshold being exceeded
questions.explain: Setting the alert below 15% free gives time to act before the disk hits 100% and the application crashes.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say an alert rule needs an Action Group (Azure) or SNS topic (AWS) attached to it?
options: An alert rule only evaluates a condition — without a notification attached, it's as useless as having no alert at all
Action Groups and SNS topics are required to create any Azure or AWS resource
They are optional extras that don't affect whether the alert works
They replace the need for a log destination entirely
questions.explain: The alert condition and the actual notification are two separate pieces that must be wired together, or the alert fires with nobody told.
